quick.prompt: With your closest person, the ideal is…

quick.b: Close, and we each keep time of our own.

scene.prompt: Think of your last free day with nothing planned. How much went to your closest person?

A good chunk, then some time to myself.
One check-in text. The rest was mine.

quick.prompt: Someone great does one small thing that gives you the ick.

Made time, but kept it on the short side.
Answered the next day and felt bad about it.
Said "not tonight" and offered another day.

scene.prompt: Think of the last time a friend went quiet for a few weeks. What went through your head?

Noticed, figured they were busy, and moved on.
Checked their posts to make sure they were okay.

quick.prompt: A close friend clearly hurt someone. The facts are pretty settled. What do you do first?

scene.prompt: Think of the last time a friend was pretty clearly wrong in group drama. What did you do?

Stayed neutral and let it blow over.
Told them privately that they'd messed up.
Said it in the group chat, kindly but clearly.

quick.prompt: Friends plan a birthday trip that's over your comfortable budget, but doable.

scene.prompt: Think of the last time friends planned something above your budget. What did you do?
options: Went, paid, and quietly cut back for a week.
Joined, but skipped the pricier parts without saying why.

scene.prompt: Think of the last time a friend asked your honest opinion on something they made. What did you say?

Said "I love it!" and let it be.

notes: Kind voice: plain, warm, first-person actions with no teasing. Every scene keeps the "Think of the last time" framing so it records what people did, and each option keeps the bank.js meaning, level and order (including celebration_budget's -2,-1,+2,+1 order and the none-level options on fairness_rule and risk_style). Warmth is spread evenly: the gentle detail goes on every option, not only the healthy-looking one (for example "Let it fade on its own" sits beside "Said something, and we talked it out", and the self-invest and help-others options both get a reason). Emotion-coded options keep their private feeling in quiet words ("felt bad about it", "quietly noticed I'd ordered less", "still think about the other", "Wondered, quietly, if they still liked me"). I removed trait words that were in the source prompts ("trust issues", "boundaries", "the mature move") and swapped rejected metaphors ("Sleep is a social construct", "a timer in my head") for true details. Options start with different words so they scan cleanly. The three 18+ tags (marriage_meaning, kids_someday, wedding_budget) plus commitment_pace stay adult-only; home_split is phrased as sharing a home with anyone, so roommates and teens fit. repair_or_release uses tension as its feel, drawn from TAG-VALIDATION-SPEC 3.4, since bank.js has no entry yet.
